record.original_question: Let f be a nonzero function in L1(R) with compact support, and suppose that f + Lambda is a tiling at some level w where Lambda is a discrete set of tempered growth, meaning that #(Lambda intersect (-r,r)) = O(r^N) as r -> +infinity for some N. Must Lambda necessarily be of the form Lambda = union from j=1 to N of (a_j Z + b_j), so that in particular Lambda has bounded density and periodic structure?

evidence.quote: Let f in L1(R) be nonzero and have compact support, and suppose that f +Lambda is a tiling at some level w, where Lambda subset R is a discrete set (not a multi-set) of tempered growth. Does it follow that Lambda is of the form (1.4), i.e. Lambda is a set of bounded density having a periodic structure?
Let us say that a set Lambda subset R has tempered growth if there is N such that #(Lambda intersect (-r,r)) = O(r^N), r -> +infinity.

We say that a set Lambda subset R has a periodic structure if it can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, namely Lambda = union from j=1 to N of (a_j Z + b_j), where a_j, b_j are real numbers and a_j > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of tempered growth if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $\#(\Lambda\cap(-r,r))=O(r^N)$ as $r\to\infty$. Say that $\Lambda$ has a periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, i.e. $\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{M}(a_j\mathbb{Z}+b_j)$ with real $b_j$ and $a_j>0$. Given $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and $w\in\mathbb{C}$, we say $f+\Lambda$ is a tiling of $\mathbb{R}$ at level $w$ if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}f(x-\lambda)=w$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, with the sum converging absolutely a.e.

Prove or disprove: if $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonzero with compact support and $f+\Lambda$ is a tiling at some level $w$ for a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of tempered growth, then $\Lambda$ must have a periodic structure (and in particular bounded density).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is presented as an open problem in the 2021 survey by Kolountzakis and Lev (Discrete Analysis) on tilings by translates of a function. The corresponding result is known when f is nonnegative (translation set must be a finite union of periodic sets), but for general L^1 compactly supported f with only tempered-growth assumption on Λ, the problem appears unresolved in available literature.

status_evidence.title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing this question among the open problems on tilings by translates with tempered-growth translation sets.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses periodic structure of tiling sets and poses the tempered-growth case as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution announced; problem listed as open.
